title: MnII–GdIII Phosphonate Cages with a Large Magnetocaloric Effect

synthesis.procedure: Compound 1 was obtained by mixing [MnII(O2CtBu)4(EtOH)]n (4; 0.1 g, 0.5 mmol), [Gd2(O2CtBu)6(HO2CtBu)6] (5Gd; 0.11 g, 0.075 mmol) and H2O3PMe (0.010 g, 0.1 mmol) in MeCN (6 mL) and EtOH (2 mL) and stirring at room temperature for 15 minutes. The resulting slurry was transferred into a 10 mL Teflon-lined autoclave, heated at 150 °C for 12 h, then cooled to room temperature at 0.05 °C min−1. Colourless prism crystals of 1 were collected.
synthesis.temperature: stirring at room temperature, then solvothermal heating at 150 °C
synthesis.time: 15 min stirring, then 12 h at 150 °C; cooling at 0.05 °C min−1
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Colourless prism crystals collected after cooling to room temperature.

properties.summary: Room-temperature χMT (104.2 emu K mol−1) is below the spin-only value (110.3 emu K mol−1 for nine s=5/2 and nine s=7/2 centres), indicating significant antiferromagnetic interactions. χT falls to about 64.3 emu K mol−1 at 2 K. Magnetization at 2 K and 7 T reaches 80.9 μB, far below saturation (108 μB) and consistent with cancellation of six Mn moments within {Mn3} triangles. Peak magnetic entropy change −ΔSm = 28.0 J kg−1 K−1 at 3 K for ΔH = 70 kG; theoretical maximum ΣR ln(2s+1) = 57.0 J kg−1 K−1 is not reached because of antiferromagnetic coupling. Demonstrated molecular magnetocaloric cooling candidate, but smaller MCE than 2.

synthesis.procedure: Compound 2 was obtained by mixing [MnII(O2CtBu)4(EtOH)]n (4; 0.1 g, 0.5 mmol), 5Gd (0.1 g, 0.07 mmol) and H2O3PCH2Ph (0.017 g, 0.1 mmol) in MeCN (8 mL) and stirring at room temperature for 15 minutes. The slurry was transferred into a 10 mL Teflon-lined autoclave, heated at 150 °C for 12 h, then cooled to room temperature at 0.05 °C min−1. Colourless sheet-shaped crystals of 2 were collected.

properties.summary: Room-temperature χMT = 64.9 emu K mol−1 matches the spin-only value (64.8) for four s=5/2 and six s=7/2 centres. χT is nearly constant to 50 K, then falls to 43.0 emu K mol−1 at 2 K, indicating weak interactions. Magnetization at 2 K (60.8 μB) approaches saturation (62 μB). Peak −ΔSm = 33.7 J kg−1 K−1 at 3 K for ΔH = 70 kG, the largest MCE of the series and attributed to weaker coupling and higher Gd density; theoretical maximum 41.8 J kg−1 K−1. Suitable for low-temperature magnetic cooling.

properties.summary: Room-temperature χMT = 111.6 emu K mol−1 matches six s=5/2 (g=2) and six DyIII (s=7/2, L=5, g=4/3) centres (calcd 110.3). χT decreases to about 63.2 emu K mol−1 at 2 K. Magnetization increases linearly after 3 T and reaches 46.8 μB at 7 T and 2 K without saturation, typical of magnetic anisotropy. Combined Dy crystal-field effects and predominantly antiferromagnetic exchange reduce the MCE: peak −ΔSm = 13.0 J kg−1 K−1 at 3 K for ΔH = 70 kG versus theoretical 42.5 J kg−1 K−1.
